CVE-2026-116265.title: MIME::Field::ParamVal versions before 5.521 for Perl do not flag an ambiguous multipart boundary written as RFC 2231 continuations
CVE-2026-116265.description:
MIME::Field::ParamVal versions before 5.521 for Perl do not flag an ambiguous multipart boundary written as RFC 2231 continuations.

The boundary ambiguity checks look only at a plain boundary= parameter, and a boundary split into RFC 2231 sections (boundary*0=, boundary*1= and so on) is joined after they have run. A repeated section number is concatenated rather than reported as a duplicate. From version 5.518, an encoded word or trailing whitespace in such a boundary also goes unflagged, although multipart_boundary() decodes or strips it.

A remote sender can make MIME::Parser split a message on a different boundary than other mail readers, hiding an attachment from a filter that relies on ambiguous_content() while the recipient's mail client shows it.

CVE-2026-131213.title: SPL Injection through Finding Exclusion Rules in Splunk Enterprise Security
CVE-2026-131213.description:
In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user who holds the "ess_analyst" Splunk Enterprise Security role could store attacker-controlled data in finding exclusion rule metadata. Another authenticated user could later open the Finding Exclusion Rules page. Splunk Enterprise Security could then run attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) commands using the permissions of the user who opened the page. The first user could access data and perform actions available to the later user.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise Security does not escape backslashes in finding exclusion rule metadata before adding the values to a page search.
For more information see Finding exclusions in Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/administer/8.7/user-and-entity-behavior-analytics/finding-exclusions-in-splunk-enterprise-security) and Users and roles for Splunk Enterprise Security…

Prior to 24.04.18 and 25.04.11, the `host_session_id` query/form parameter is substituted into the `cool.html` editor page without HTML encoding, unlike parameters passed through the existing variable-encoding mechanism. CVE-2026-81938.title: Arbitrary file read via Alertmanager receiver configuration in Grafana Mimir
CVE-2026-81938.description:
Grafana Mimir's Alertmanager rejects tenant-supplied receiver configurations that reference local files, but the check did not cover two HTTP client settings: http_headers.<name>.files and basic_auth.username_file. A tenant permitted to upload an Alertmanager configuration could point these fields at any file readable by the Alertmanager process. When a notification was sent, Alertmanager read the file and put its contents in a header of the outgoing request. By directing the receiver at a server they control, the tenant could read files from the Alertmanager host, such as credentials and configuration.

Exploitation requires permission to write the tenant's Alertmanager configuration. Grafana Enterprise Metrics (GEM), which is built on Mimir, is also affected. The issue is fixed in Mimir 3.1.7 and 3.2.2 and in GEM 2.17.20. GEM 2.11 through 2.16 will not receive a fix; users on those versions should upgrade to 2.17.20 or later.

CVE-2026-94565.description: NukeViet CMS is a multi Content Management System. From the 3.x release line until 4.6.01, an unauthenticated visitor can submit a Contact module message containing an event-handler attribute prefixed by a slash. NukeViet\Core\Request::filterTags() tokenizes attributes using only ASCII spaces, so it sees /onerror and misses the ^on denylist, while the browser treats the slash as a separator and activates onerror. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.01.

CVE-2026-99438.title: media: rc: mce_kbd: Fix inconsistent locking of keylock
CVE-2026-99438.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

media: rc: mce_kbd: Fix inconsistent locking of keylock

data->keylock is taken with spin_lock() in ir_mce_kbd_decode(), which
runs in the raw IR decode kthread with local interrupts enabled, but
with spin_lock_irqsave() in mce_kbd_rx_timeout(), the rx_timeout timer
callback, which runs in softirq context.

If the decode kthread is holding keylock via spin_lock() when a timer
interrupt fires on the same CPU and the softirq runs
mce_kbd_rx_timeout(), the softirq spins forever waiting for a lock
that only the now-preempted kthread can release, while the kthread
cannot run again until the softirq gives up the CPU. This deadlocks
the CPU.

ceph: fail readdir when the MDS reply carries no dirfrag

request with a reply whose extra blob is empty. parse_reply_info()

/* extra */

...
}

In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

drm/drm_crtc: ensure dma_fence_ops remain valid during device unbind

In [1], sashiko reported the following issue:

=== snip ===
Looking at how these fences are managed, drm_crtc_create_fence()
creates a dma_fence without taking a reference to the drm_device or
drm_crtc. Because the sync_file framework exposes this fence to
userspace, the fence can outlive the CRTC.

The dma_fence contract requires that data accessed by dma_fence_ops
(like get_driver_name) must remain valid for an RCU grace period after
the fence is signaled. However, drm_crtc_cleanup() and the subsequent
freeing of the device do not wait for an RCU grace period via
synchronize_rcu().

sync_file_get_name()

// Preempted or delayed here
